_comment: DIFFICULTY AXIS on the new-rule rung: demos per instance.
The k axis is the natural difficulty knob for anything that must be induced
rather than recalled, and it has never been swept -- every new-rule run so
far pooled k in {1,2,3,5} into a single number.
Why paired with k-axis-constant-rule.json rather than run alone: if held-out
accuracy is flat in k HERE, that is uninterpretable on its own. It is
interpretable next to the same-rule rung, where transfer is known to exist
and rises with data. More evidence helping there and not here is a
k=0 is a real point, not a formality: it carries no rule in the prompt, so
it measures pure recall of the trained rule. The gap between k=0 and k>=1 is
what evidence in context is worth, measured rather than assumed.
Read with off_pair_rate, not byte accuracy alone. On a 3-symbol alphabet
chance is 0.333, so a weak partial competence cannot be told from guessing;
off_pair cannot be gamed by a positional bias.
